requirement:
When replacing results for an unfiltered workspace invocation or a filtered
invocation selecting at least one test, a prepared build configuration
incompatible with the active configuration under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` clears the whole
current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test
execution.

Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that
configuration is selected again. A filtered invocation selecting no tests
leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration_reset`. I did not read the implementation, because the tests' assertions were enough to judge them.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

- **Filtered invocation selecting at least one test, incompatible configuration.** `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[incompatible_builds_reset_every_test_but_empty_focused_runs_do_not]` first stores two tests under configuration "a" and completes one with measurements. A filtered replace under configuration "b" selecting only `selected[0]` follows. The test asserts that the configuration becomes "b", that exactly one test remains, and that it is pending with no measurements. The unselected test was cleared, so the whole set was cleared and not only the selected identities.
- **Unfiltered invocation, incompatible configuration.** The same test stores and completes two tests under "a". An unfiltered replace under "b" selecting only the first test follows. It asserts the configuration is "b", one test remains, and that test is pending with no measurements. The unselected second test's completed result is gone.
- **Previous results do not reappear when that configuration is selected again.** The test switches back to "a" with a filtered replace selecting only `selected[1]`. It asserts exactly one test, named "b", with no measurements. Test "a" had earlier completed results under "a", and they did not come back.
- **Filtered invocation selecting no tests leaves results and active configuration unchanged.** The test calls `replace` with an incompatible configuration "b" and an empty filtered selection. It asserts the call returns false and that the snapshot still shows configuration "a", both tests, and their measurements. Only the latest invocation changes, as `storage.replace` allows.
- **Reset and activation in the same atomic replacement.** `fn[failed_atomic_replacement_preserves_results_configuration_and_invocation]` forces an insert failure with a trigger during an incompatible-configuration replace. It asserts that the configuration, latest invocation, test identity and measurements all stay as before. The new configuration therefore does not become active apart from the results clear.
- **Before test execution.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[a_failed_replacement_commit_reports_the_error_without_launching_execution]` runs an end-to-end `habeas coverage` with `--features alpha`, which is incompatible with the earlier run. A synthetic commit failure makes the replacement fail. The test asserts that the command fails, that stderr reports the failure, that the `cargo nextest run` sentinel never started, and that the stored runs and measurements are unchanged. This shows the replacement commits before execution begins.

**Other points**

- The `storage.replace` clauses about fail-fast, the compatible-configuration filtered preserve case, and commit-failure reporting belong to that requirement and its tests. The cited `storage.configuration` compatibility rule is context, not something to reassess here.
- I found no unmarked relevant tests and no inadequate assertions, so there is no gap and no FIXME is needed.

text: :::{req} storage.configuration_reset
When replacing results for an unfiltered workspace invocation or a filtered
invocation selecting at least one test, a prepared build configuration
incompatible with the active configuration under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` clears the whole
current set and becomes active in the same atomic replacement, before test
execution.
Results from the previous configuration do not reappear when that
configuration is selected again. A filtered invocation selecting no tests
leaves the current results and active configuration unchanged under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`.
:::{req} storage.configuration
Each coverage record MUST identify the recorded toolchain, compilation target,
Cargo build profile, enabled features, and instrumentation-affecting compiler
settings. These settings MUST determine build-configuration compatibility for
the combined view. A nextest scheduling profile alone MUST NOT make otherwise
compatible build configurations incompatible.
:::{req} storage.replace
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:
- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
`habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.
Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.
A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.
If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
